_scope_note: Raising the floors edits exactly one effective map: package.json's pnpm.overrides. pnpm-workspace.yaml is NOT in scope and must not be edited - see negative_scope. pnpm-lock.yaml is regenerated, never hand-edited. osv-scanner.toml is in scope only to delete one dead IgnoredVulns entry. The slice doc and this manifest are in scope on purpose (AP-39/AP-40 lesson).
negative_scope: NEVER edit pnpm-workspace.yaml. Measured 2026-08-03 (pnpm 10.30.2, docs/standards/dependency-override-precedence.md): when package.json declares a NON-EMPTY pnpm.overrides map, it REPLACES pnpm-workspace.yaml's overrides map entirely - a whole-map replacement, not a per-key merge. This repo's package.json map is non-empty, so every key in pnpm-workspace.yaml's overrides block is already dropped at resolution time. Adding a floor there would be inert and would look fixed while changing nothing - the exact failure this repo already paid for once with esbuild.

NEVER lower, delete or per-invoke override minimumReleaseAge, trustPolicy or blockExoticSubdeps in pnpm-workspace.yaml. Owner decision 2026-07-26 (backlog task deps-security-bump): the 7-day window exists to block the hijacked-publish vector for which a fake security patch is the classic carrier; trading that control for a few days of earlier patching on a zero-exposure surface is a bad trade. If a target version is still inside the window, SPLIT THAT PACKAGE OUT of this slice - do not wait inside the slice and do not override.

NO unrelated dependency upgrades riding along. Only the three packages named in _target_floors may change resolved version. Any other version delta in pnpm-lock.yaml is scope drift and must be reverted or reported.
NO hand-editing pnpm-lock.yaml. It is regenerated by pnpm install and reviewed as output.

NO new IgnoredVulns entry in osv-scanner.toml. That file's own policy is 'an entry here is a REACHABILITY argument, never a convenience mute'. This slice only DELETES a dead entry; if a floor cannot be raised, split the package out rather than muting it.
NO edit to .github/workflows/security.yml or ci.yml. The scanner configuration is not the defect.

_brace_expansion_v1_note: The 2026-07-29 owner decision split brace-expansion out of deps-security-bump because forcing v1 to v5 breaks at runtime: v1 is `module.exports = expandTop` (a function) while v5 is CJS `exports.expand` (an object), and its only consumer minimatch@3.1.5 calls it as a function. Measured 2026-08-10 at 9d7d6ac: `grep -c 'brace-expansion@1\.' pnpm-lock.yaml` returns 0 - the v1 branch is GONE, removed by the eslint 9->10 migration (a93a4f6) exactly as that decision predicted. The trap therefore does not apply here. RE-MEASURE before relying on this; if any v1 entry has returned, brace-expansion splits out again. Re-measured 2026-08-11 at 005a44e: still 0 (only brace-expansion@5.0.7 remains, lock lines 1145/2747; the `brace-expansion@1: ^1.1.16` guard is intact at line 8). Trap stays expired; a plain 5.x floor is safe.
